text.paragraph: Primary care survivorship visit five and a half months after right mastectomy for stage IA breast cancer, on tamoxifen. Concerns: Moving her breast cancer survivorship care to primary care, with the oncology team kept informed; mild hot flashes on tamoxifen; Wants complete information and to make her own decisions. She chose a flat closure without reconstruction and does not wish to wear an external prosthesis; she asks that this not be raised again unless she raises it. [S]

tr.td: Tamoxifen 20 mg oral tablet, one tablet by mouth once daily, planned for at least five years

value.displayName: Malignant neoplasm of upper-outer quadrant of right female breast
Long term (current) use of selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs)

tr.td: Diagnostic bilateral mammography after a self-detected right breast lump: 1.6 cm irregular mass in the upper outer right breast, BI-RADS 5; left breast normal
Right breast and axillary ultrasound: 1.6 cm irregular hypoechoic mass at 10 o'clock; normal axillary lymph nodes
Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy of the right breast mass: invasive ductal carcinoma, grade 2; ER 90 percent, PR 60 percent, HER2 1+ (negative), Ki-67 12 percent

Right total mastectomy with flat closure and no reconstruction, her informed choice. Pathology: invasive ductal carcinoma 1.6 cm, grade 2, margins clear, no lymphovascular invasion; pT1c pN0(sn), stage IA. Recurrence score (21-gene assay) 14
Right axillary sentinel lymph node biopsy at mastectomy: 0 of 2 nodes involved
Diagnostic mammography of the left breast one year after diagnosis: scattered fibroglandular tissue, no suspicious findings, BI-RADS 1
Genetic counseling for hereditary breast cancer risk: pedigree taken and multigene panel testing for inherited cancer risk sent; result pending at the end of the episode
Cervical sampling for cytology with human papillomavirus co-testing; result pending at the end of the episode

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Medical oncology consultation to confirm the adjuvant endocrine therapy plan, advise on hot flashes, set the surveillance plan, and advise on genetic assessment
Tamoxifen 20 mg daily for at least five years, with questions at every visit about hot flashes, abnormal vaginal bleeding, and leg swelling or breathlessness, and a yearly gynecologic assessment

Cancer-related history and examination every 3 to 6 months for the first 3 years and a yearly diagnostic mammogram of the left breast; no routine blood tests, tumor markers, or body imaging while she has no symptoms
Germline genetic counseling and multigene panel testing for breast cancer diagnosed at 44
Lymphedema risk counseling and arm checks at every visit; bone health by calcium and vitamin D from diet and weight-bearing exercise; distress, depression, and anxiety screening at intervals
Written survivorship care plan, at least 150 minutes of activity a week, alcohol at or below one drink a day, and her decisions about reconstruction and a prosthesis recorded and respected
Continue tamoxifen daily with side effects she finds tolerable
Taking it daily; mild hot flashes controlled without medicine; no abnormal bleeding or clot symptoms
Complete the yearly surveillance mammogram of the left breast
Left mammogram one year after diagnosis: BI-RADS 1
Complete germline genetic assessment, missed at diagnosis
Genetic counseling completed and panel testing sent; result pending
Keep at least 150 minutes of activity a week and a stable weight
Walking about 200 minutes a week; weight stable at 71 to 72 kg
